title: Shared Family Definitions
description: Definitions shared byte-for-byte between primitive_families.schema.json and mode_families.schema.json, factored out here so they are defined once. Anything that transitively depends on a family's tier-specific 'characteristics' shape (e.g. 'instance') stays local to each of those two schemas instead of living here.

influence.description: Records genuine design lineage from source_family_id to this family, not general co-occurrence in a paper. Only add one when the cited source states a concretely reused or adapted component (S-box, key schedule, round function, permutation, whitening construction, round constants, etc.), explicit 'based on'/'derived from'/'inspired by'/'generalizes'/'extends' language about the design itself, or literal same-team continuation of an earlier design. Do NOT record an influence, even if the source discusses it at length, for: a pure performance/benchmark comparison ('we compare cycle count to X', 'faster than X'); 'positioned against'/'contrasted with'/'designed to avoid a weakness of X' framing where nothing is adopted; a shared target application or use case ('also lightweight'); a shared abstract paradigm with no concretely borrowed mechanism ('both ARX', 'both Feistel', 'both sponge-based') -- this applies even when the source self-categorizes this way; a related-work listing that merely enumerates several earlier designs sharing a generic technique without singling one out as the actual adopted basis; or anything the source states was developed independently. When unsure, omit the edge -- a missed influence is far cheaper to add later than a fabricated one is to catch. See the 'Contributing' section of README.md for the full rule and worked examples.
